note: First eval against production deployment. Scores largely match localhost eval from earlier today — validates that deployed site matches dev.

hierarchy.evidence: Homepage: H1 88px serif dominates, sage CTA clear primary, subtitle well-receded. Services: 'Most Popular' badge + featured card layout creates clear priority. About: image + stats create strong visual path. Contact: redundant 'Get in touch' H1 + H2.
hierarchy.prescription: Contact page: differentiate H1 from H2 — H1 should be the emotional hook, H2 the functional label

breathing_room.evidence: Homepage: generous 80-112px section padding, hero has room to breathe. Services: featured card has good internal padding, secondary cards well-spaced. About: photo-to-text spacing balanced. Footer: 3-column with adequate margins.
breathing_room.prescription: Services secondary cards could use slightly more vertical gap between them

contrast.evidence: Homepage: sage CTA on cream works, bark text on cream high contrast, trust strip legible. Services: price/duration tags clear. About: stat numbers (10+, 1:1) pop with serif weight. Weakness: nav items all same weight, no active-state differentiation on desktop.
contrast.prescription: Add font-weight or underline to active nav item on desktop — currently no visual indication which page you're on

polish.evidence: Homepage: GSAP parallax hero, staggered fade-in-up, custom ::selection, prefers-reduced-motion. About page image NOW WORKING (was broken grey rectangle). Services booking widget with stars. API/track endpoint throwing 500 on every page load. Clerk loaded in dev mode on production.
polish.prescription: Fix /api/track 500 error — visible in console on every page. Switch Clerk to production keys.

emotional_tone.evidence: Homepage: 'Move Better. Feel Better. Live Better.' has great rhythm. Real testimonial. Instagram CTA feels personal. About: Chelsea's story is authentic — burnout, pivot, purpose. 'Your presence is your power' quote anchors it. Contact: hours + embedded map feel complete and trustworthy.
emotional_tone.prescription: Homepage Instagram section feels thin — just a link. Show 2-3 actual Instagram photos to build emotional connection

information_density.evidence: Homepage: appropriate — hero sparse, trust strip dense but scannable. Services: excellent density — featured card with full details, secondary cards with price/duration/audience. Contact: good balance of info + map. FAQ page content not evaluated but nav-reachable.
information_density.prescription: Homepage could benefit from a 'Why stretching?' educational snippet between trust strip and CTA

wayfinding.evidence: Every page ends with 'Ready to feel better?' CTA — no dead ends. 8-item nav reaches all pages. Footer duplicates full nav + contact. Services active state visible. Skip-to-content link present. Weakness: no breadcrumbs, active nav state subtle.
wayfinding.prescription: Bold or underline current page in nav — currently relies only on text-transform which is subtle

distinctiveness.evidence: Public site: Instrument Serif + cream/sage/bark palette is ownable. Real hero photo of studio (not stock). Trust strip with real credentials. About page photo is Chelsea herself. But: inner pages (Services, Contact, FAQ) feel like well-executed template — grid cards, standard layout patterns.
distinctiveness.prescription: Services page needs one Chelsea-specific visual element — a photo of her working with a client, or the studio space. Currently all text, no imagery.

scroll_experience.evidence: Homepage: 5 sections (hero, trust strip, testimonial, Instagram, CTA) — variety exists but total scroll is short. GSAP ScrollTrigger active. Services page has best depth — featured card, service grid, booking widget, testimonials. About has nice photo-to-text reveal.
scroll_experience.prescription: Homepage needs 1-2 more content blocks — a brief 'How it works' or 'Who it's for' section between trust strip and testimonial

layout_coherence.evidence: Consistent max-width container across all pages. Header/footer shared. Section padding follows 80/96/112px scale. Services uses 2-column featured + card grid. About uses 2-column photo + text. Contact uses 2-column info + map. All stack cleanly on mobile 390px.
layout_coherence.prescription: Minor: Services secondary cards use slightly different internal padding than featured card — normalize the padding scale

information_architecture.evidence: 8 nav items all reachable, all return 200. Logical grouping: Services, About, Events, Providers, FAQ, Shop, Contact, Book Now. Book Now links to /services#booking (not a separate page — smart). Per-page titles set correctly. No orphan routes found. No dead links detected in production.
information_architecture.prescription: Consider grouping Events + Providers under an 'Explore' dropdown — 8 top-level items is at Hick's law threshold

evidence: Real Chelsea photo in hero and about
Google Maps embed with real address

gestalt.see: Full-bleed studio photo with warm cream overlay, large serif 'Move Better' headline dominates left half, sage 'Book a Session' CTA. Immediate clarity: this is a wellness business in a real space.
gestalt.feel: Warm, personal, trustworthy. Feels like a real person's business, not a template. The serif + cream palette signals 'premium wellness' without being cold or corporate.
gestalt.wrong: /api/track 500 error in console on every page. Nav has 8 items with no visual active state on desktop. Homepage scroll is short — only 5 sections before footer.

confidence: medium — first production eval, partially calibrated (2/3), previous localhost evals provide baseline

errors.finding: /api/track returns 500 on every page load — analytics tracking broken in production
Clerk loaded with development keys on production deployment (console warning)

accessibility.images_alt: FAIL — hero image missing alt text (studio-wide.webp)

mobile.hero_responsive: CTAs stack vertically, text scales down, image fills viewport

feature_context.for: Chelsea Rohl (solo practitioner) and her potential clients

opportunities.finding: Book a Session CTA appears 3x (hero, nav, every page footer) — good repetition
Real testimonials, real photo, real address with map — trust signals are genuine
No imagery on Services page — all text descriptions of physical services. A photo of a stretch session would dramatically increase conversion.
Instagram section is just a link — no preview content. Missed opportunity to show social proof visually.
